decision_records.decision: Extend the EXISTING buildNewInitializerMap brace-tracking pass into a scope-binding module rather than building parallel machinery
decision_records.rationale: classifyMethodCall branch 3 + NewInitializerMap already implement the const x = new Y() scope-stack pattern (module-private type, safe to reshape). Gaps found in T1: (1) class METHOD bodies never get scope frames, so bindings inside methods are silently dropped - the largest coverage hole; (2) no let/var; (3) no TS type-annotated declarations (const x: Foo); (4) no typed parameters (function f(x: Foo)).

decision_records.decision: Bindings carry provenance kind (new | annotation | param); resolution strictness varies by kind
decision_records.rationale: new-expression bindings are PROVEN instances: own-methods miss returns unresolved (method_not_in_class_own_methods), current semantics. annotation/param bindings may name interfaces or supertypes: own-methods miss FALLS THROUGH to the field-index ACG tail instead of returning, so no existing provisional resolution is lost (no-regress guard). Successful annotation/param matches resolve at FULL confidence with reason scope_binding_annotation / scope_binding_param - the annotation is declared truth modulo subtyping.

cross-file dataflow inference; factory returns (const x = makeY()); reassignment tracking (x = new Z() after decl - first binding wins per scope, existing guardrail 2); generics narrowing (Foo<T> strips to Foo); union/intersection annotations (skipped); interface member resolution (interfaces are single elements, not method-bearing); destructuring; Python (JS/TS only, language-guarded like all prior reclassify work). No new edge KIND is introduced - resolved-call evidence only, so adjacency indexes need no change.

metrics_diff.honest_assessment: PLAN.md framed this class at 62%/10,691 from a stale scan; the live class was 7,699 and is dominated by receiver shapes scope-binding CANNOT address by design: dotted receivers 5,050 (65% - expect(result), vi.fn(), z.string(), new Date()) and test-framework vocabulary. Local class-instance receivers - the Stack-Graphs pattern - are structurally rare in this repo. The pass ships correct and tested; its ceiling HERE is low, and its value scales with codebases that use typed locals over factories/namespaces.
